software_info.name: GEM-pRF
software_info.full_name: GPU-Empowered Mapping of Population Receptive Fields
software_info.author: Siddharth Mittal
software_info.paper_title: GPU-Empowered Mapping of Population Receptive Fields for Large-Scale fMRI Analysis
software_info.description: GEM-pRF is a software for population receptive field (pRF) mapping using GPU acceleration. It analyzes fMRI data to map how visual cortex processes different regions of visual space.
software_info.purpose: Map population receptive fields in visual cortex using fMRI data with GPU acceleration
software_info.support: For installation help, bug reports, troubleshooting, or general usage questions, please visit the support page or contact the author.
software_info.scope_note: This chatbot only answers questions about XML configuration file parameters. For other topics, visit the documentation.

ui_elements.description: UI elements and their corresponding XML parameters. This section helps map user interface labels to XML configuration parameters.

config_filename_builder.name: Config Filename Builder
config_filename_builder.description: A UI-only feature (not part of XML) that helps users create descriptive filenames for configuration files. It combines Data Source, Stimulus Type, and Description fields to generate a meaningful filename.

components.data_source: Identifier for your data source (e.g., HCP, NYU). Max 5 words.
components.stimulus_type: Type of stimulus used (e.g., fixed bar). Max 5 words.
components.description: Brief analysis description (e.g., high res analysis). Max 10 words.

config_filename_builder.note: This is not a configuration parameter - it's a helper tool to name your config file.

version.description: The version of the configuration file format. Currently fixed at 0.1.11. This determines the XML structure.

enable_refine_fitting.description: Checkbox to enable/disable refine fitting. GEM-pRF uses one-step refine fitting based on quadratic approximation.

execute_on_gpu.description: Checkbox to execute refine fitting on GPU for faster processing.

stimulus_directory.description: Path to directory containing stimulus files in Nifti format.

visual_field_radius.description: Radius of visual field in degrees (e.g., 8 means ±8 degrees).

width.description: Width of stimulus image in pixels.

height.description: Height of stimulus image in pixels.

enable_binarization.description: Enable binarization of stimulus images using a threshold.

threshold.description: Threshold value for binarization. Pixels above this value become 1, below become 0.

enable.description: Enable high temporal resolution mode for stimulus processing.

slice_time_ref.description: Slice timing reference for temporal alignment (0-1, typically 0.5 for middle slice).

input_data_source.description: Choose between BIDS format (structured neuroimaging data) or Fixed Paths (manual file paths).

data_organization_type.bids_format: Use BIDS-compliant data structure with automatic file discovery
data_organization_type.fixed_paths: Manually specify exact file paths for stimulus and measured data

run_type.description: Individual (analyze runs separately) or Concatenated (combine multiple runs).

base_path.description: Root directory of your BIDS dataset.

append_to_base_path.description: Folders to append to base path (comma-separated, e.g., 'derivatives,fmriprep').

results_analysis_id.description: Custom ID for results folder (e.g., '01' creates 'analysis-01').

overwrite_existing_results.description: Checkbox to allow overwriting existing analysis results.

hemisphere.description: Hemisphere to process: L, R, or 'all'.

space.description: Coordinate space(s): fsnative, fsaverage, T1w, or 'all'.

task.description: Single task name (e.g., 'fixedbar'). Do not use 'all'.

concatenated_analysis.description: Combine multiple runs into single analysis. Each item specifies ses, task, and run to concatenate.

concatenate_items.description: List of items to concatenate, each with ses, task, and run values.

measured_data_file_paths.description: List of full paths to measured fMRI data files (.nii.gz).

results_base_path.description: Directory where analysis results will be saved.

custom_filename_postfix.description: Custom text added to result filenames (e.g., '-sample').

prepend_date_to_filename.description: Checkbox to add date prefix to result filenames.

model_type.description: Type of pRF model. Currently only '2D Gaussian' is available. DoG and CSS models not yet implemented.

batches.description: Number of batches for processing data. Adjust based on available GPU memory.

default_gpu.description: Default GPU index (0 for first GPU, 1 for second, etc.).

additional_available_gpus.description: List of additional GPU indices available for processing.

search_space.description: The Search Space section defines all parameters for the grid search phase of pRF fitting, including HRF parameters, spatial grid, sigma values, and drift removal.

write_debug.description: Checkbox to save debug information during grid search.

optional_analysis_parameters.description: Load custom HRF, sigmas, or spatial grid from an external file instead of using default values.

use_custom_parameters.description: Checkbox to load parameters from external .h5 file.

file_path.description: Path to .h5 file containing custom parameters.

use_hrf_from_file.description: Load HRF values from file instead of computing from default parameters.

hrf_key.description: Key/path in .h5 file for HRF values (e.g., 'analysis_params/hrf_values').

use_sigmas_from_file.description: Load sigma values from file instead of using default range.

sigmas_key.description: Key/path in .h5 file for sigma values (e.g., 'analysis_params/sigmas').

use_spatial_grid_from_file.description: Load spatial grid positions from file instead of using default grid.

spatial_grid_key.description: Key/path in .h5 file for spatial grid (e.g., 'analysis_params/spatial_grid_xy').

default_hrf_parameters.description: Hemodynamic Response Function parameters for modeling BOLD response. These define the shape of the HRF used in pRF fitting.

time_range_t.description: Time range for HRF in seconds (e.g., '(0, 45)' for 0 to 45 seconds).

tr.description: Repetition Time in seconds (time between volume acquisitions).

peak_delay.description: Time to peak of HRF in seconds.

undershoot_delay.description: Time to undershoot of HRF in seconds.

peak_to_undershoot_ratio.description: Ratio of peak amplitude to undershoot amplitude.

normalize_hrf.description: Checkbox to normalize HRF to unit sum.

default_spatial_grid.description: Grid of pRF center positions to search during grid search phase.

visual_field_radius.description: Maximum eccentricity in degrees for pRF centers.

number_of_horizontal_prfs.description: Number of pRF positions along horizontal axis.

number_of_vertical_prfs.description: Number of pRF positions along vertical axis.

default_sigmas.description: Range of pRF sizes (sigma values in degrees) to search during grid search.

number_of_sigmas.description: Number of different sigma values to test.

ndct.description: Discrete Cosine Transform bases for removing low-frequency drift from fMRI signals.

ndct_value.description: Number of DCT bases for low-frequency drift removal. Generates (2*nDCT + 1) cosine regressors.

enable.explanation: Controls whether refine fitting is performed after the initial grid search. GEM-pRF uses a one-step refine fitting based on quadratic approximation to fine-tune pRF parameters.
enable.use_case: Enable for more accurate pRF estimates. Uses one-step quadratic approximation refinement after grid search.

refinefit_on_gpu.explanation: If enabled, refine fitting computations will be executed on GPU hardware. This significantly speeds up the fitting process if sufficient GPU memory is available.
refinefit_on_gpu.use_case: Enable if you have a GPU with sufficient VRAM (typically 8GB+). Disable if you have limited GPU memory or want to use CPU only.

directory.explanation: Path to the directory containing your stimulus files. These should be in Nifti format (.nii.gz). The stimulus represents the visual stimuli presented during the fMRI experiment.
directory.use_case: Point to the folder where your aperture/stimulus files are stored. These are typically 3D arrays where each frame represents a different stimulus aperture position.

visual_field.explanation: The radius of the visual field in degrees. This defines the extent of the visual stimulus space (e.g., ±8 degrees means the stimulus covers 16x16 degrees of visual angle).
visual_field.use_case: Set this based on your actual stimulus. Common values are 8° (standard) or 12° (larger field).

width.explanation: The width of the stimulus image in pixels. This should match the horizontal dimension of your stimulus files.
width.use_case: 101x101 is standard for most pRF studies. Adjust if your stimulus has different dimensions.

height.explanation: The height of the stimulus image in pixels. This should match the vertical dimension of your stimulus files.
height.use_case: Usually matches width for square stimuli. Set to your actual stimulus dimensions.

binarization_enable.explanation: When enabled, stimulus values are converted to binary (0 and 1). All values above the threshold become 1, all values below become 0. This can help with noisy stimulus data.
binarization_enable.use_case: Enable if your stimulus is noisy or has intermediate values. Disable if you want to preserve stimulus intensity variations.

binarization_threshold.explanation: The threshold value used for binarization. Stimulus values above this threshold are set to 1, below are set to 0.
binarization_threshold.use_case: Set to 0 if using a binary stimulus (0 and 1). Adjust if you have grayscale stimulus data.

high_temporal_resolution.explanation: Enable this to compute model signals using high-resolution stimulus and then downsample to match your fMRI temporal resolution. This improves stimulus sampling accuracy.
high_temporal_resolution.use_case: Enable if your stimulus has very fast changes or high frame rate. Useful for stimulus-locked designs.

num_frames_downsampled.explanation: The number of fMRI frames in your timecourse. This is the total length of your fMRI time series (number of TRs).
num_frames_downsampled.use_case: Set this to match the total number of volumes/TRs in your fMRI data.

slice_time_ref.explanation: Slice timing reference (0.0 to 1.0). Controls how stimulus-fMRI alignment is handled when slices are acquired at different times. 0.5 means the reference is at the middle of the TR.
slice_time_ref.use_case: Use 0.5 for most cases. Adjust if you need precise temporal alignment accounting for slice acquisition order.

BIDS_enable.explanation: When enabled, GEM-pRF expects data organized in BIDS (Brain Imaging Data Structure) format. This is the recommended and most flexible approach.
BIDS_enable.use_case: Enable if your data follows BIDS format. Disable only if using fixed file paths instead.

BIDS_run_type.explanation: Specifies how multiple runs are handled. 'individual' analyzes each run separately. 'concatenated' combines multiple runs before analysis.
BIDS_run_type.use_case: Use 'individual' if runs have different stimulus conditions. Use 'concatenated' to pool data from multiple runs for more statistical power.

basepath.explanation: The root path to your BIDS dataset. All relative paths are resolved from here.
basepath.use_case: Point to the top-level BIDS directory containing sub-* folders.

append_to_basepath.explanation: Additional path components to append to the basepath. Useful for pointing to preprocessed data in derivatives folders.
append_to_basepath.use_case: Use 'derivatives, fmriprep' if your preprocessed fMRI data is in BIDS/derivatives/fmriprep.

results_anaylsis_id.explanation: Directory name for storing analysis results. If overwrite=False, a timestamp is appended to avoid overwriting previous results.
results_anaylsis_id.use_case: Use a descriptive name like 'MyStudy_pRF_Analysis' to organize results.

results_overwrite.explanation: When False, results are saved with a timestamp suffix to prevent overwriting. When True, existing results are replaced.
results_overwrite.use_case: Keep False during development. Set to True only when you're sure you want to replace results.

analysis.explanation: Which analysis run numbers to process. Use comma-separated values (e.g., '01, 02') or 'all' for all runs.
analysis.use_case: Set to specific run numbers for testing, or 'all' for complete analysis.

sub.explanation: Which subjects to analyze. Use comma-separated subject IDs or 'all' for all subjects in the dataset.
sub.use_case: Use specific subject IDs during testing, 'all' for group analysis.

hemi.explanation: Which brain hemispheres to process. Options are 'left', 'right', or 'all' for both hemispheres.
hemi.use_case: Use 'all' for bilateral analysis. Use 'left' or 'right' if studying specific hemisphere.

space.explanation: Which anatomical space your data is in. Examples: 'fsnative' (native surface), 'fsaverage' (standard average), 'T1w' (native anatomical), 'MNI152NLin2009cAsym', etc.
space.use_case: Use 'fsnative' for subject-specific surface. Use 'fsaverage' for standard template space. Use 'all' to process all available spaces.

input_file_extension.explanation: File format of input fMRI data. '.gii' for surface files (GIFTI), '.nii.gz' for volumetric files (Nifti), 'both' to accept either format.
input_file_extension.use_case: Use '.gii' for surface-based analysis (recommended). Use '.nii.gz' for volumetric analysis.

individual_task.explanation: The specific fMRI task name to analyze when using individual (non-concatenated) runs. Must be exactly one value.

individual_ses.explanation: Session labels for individual analysis. Use comma-separated values or 'all'.
individual_ses.use_case: Use 'all' if you want all sessions, or specify particular session IDs.

individual_run.explanation: Run numbers for individual analysis. Use comma-separated values or 'all'.
individual_run.use_case: Use 'all' to include all runs, or specify which runs to process.

model.explanation: The receptive field model to use. Currently only '2d_gaussian' is fully available. DoG (Difference of Gaussians) and CSS (Compressive Spatial Summation) are not yet available.
model.use_case: Use '2d_gaussian' for standard pRF analysis. This models each voxel's visual receptive field as a 2D Gaussian in visual space.

batches.explanation: Number of data batches for processing. Larger values use more GPU memory but can be faster. Adjust based on your GPU VRAM.
batches.use_case: Start with 500. Increase if you have >16GB GPU VRAM. Decrease if you get out-of-memory errors.

default_gpu.explanation: Index of the primary GPU to use for computations. GPU numbering starts from 0 (first GPU).
default_gpu.use_case: Set to 0 for single GPU systems. Set to 1, 2, etc. if you have multiple GPUs and want to use a specific one.

additional_available_gpus.explanation: List of additional GPU indices available for distributed processing. These GPUs can be used for parallel analysis of multiple subjects/runs.
additional_available_gpus.use_case: List all GPU IDs you want GEM-pRF to use for parallel processing. Useful for multi-GPU setups.

write_debug_info.explanation: When enabled, generates detailed debug information during analysis. Useful for troubleshooting but increases computation time and storage.
write_debug_info.use_case: Enable only during debugging. Disable for production analysis to save time and disk space.

optional_analysis_params_enable.explanation: When enabled, GEM-pRF loads custom HRF, pRF sizes, and spatial grid from an external HDF5 file instead of using default values.
optional_analysis_params_enable.use_case: Enable if you have pre-computed or custom HRF and grid parameters. Otherwise, use defaults.

optional_analysis_params_filepath.explanation: Path to HDF5 file containing custom analysis parameters (HRF, sigma values, spatial grid).
optional_analysis_params_filepath.use_case: Provide path to your custom parameters file if optional_analysis_params_enable=True.

hrf_use_from_file.explanation: When enabled, loads custom HRF (Hemodynamic Response Function) from file. The HRF characterizes how neural activity is transformed into fMRI signal.
hrf_use_from_file.use_case: Keep True if using optional params file. Otherwise, use default HRF.

hrf_t.explanation: Time range for HRF computation in seconds. (0, 45) means HRF is computed from 0 to 45 seconds after stimulus onset.
hrf_t.use_case: Standard value (0, 45) works for most fMRI studies. Adjust if you have different TR or need different time window.

hrf_TR.explanation: Repetition Time (TR) in seconds. This is the time between successive fMRI acquisitions.
hrf_TR.use_case: Set to your actual TR. Common values: 1.0s, 1.5s, 2.0s, 3.0s depending on your acquisition protocol.

hrf_peak_delay.explanation: Time to peak of the HRF in seconds. Default SPM value is 6.16s, which is typical for visual cortex.
hrf_peak_delay.use_case: Use 6.16 for standard visual cortex. Adjust if studying other brain regions with different HRF dynamics.

hrf_under_shoot_delay.explanation: Time to the undershoot (negative deflection) of the HRF in seconds. Default is 12.0s.
hrf_under_shoot_delay.use_case: Standard SPM value 12.0s works well for most studies. Adjust based on your HRF model.

default_spatial_grid_visual_field_radius.explanation: Radius of the visual field search space in degrees. This defines the extent of pRF positions to search. Should match or exceed your stimulus visual field size.
default_spatial_grid_visual_field_radius.use_case: Set to match or exceed your visual_field stimulus parameter. Use 12° for most studies.

default_spatial_grid_num_horizontal_prfs.explanation: Number of pRF positions to sample along the horizontal axis. More values = finer grid = longer computation.
default_spatial_grid_num_horizontal_prfs.use_case: 51 is standard and provides good balance. Use 41 for faster testing, 61 for higher resolution.

default_spatial_grid_num_vertical_prfs.explanation: Number of pRF positions to sample along the vertical axis. Should typically match num_horizontal_prfs for square grid.
default_spatial_grid_num_vertical_prfs.use_case: Usually matches num_horizontal_prfs. Adjust symmetrically for balanced grid coverage.

default_sigmas_num_sigmas.explanation: Number of different pRF size (sigma) values to search. More values = more thorough search but slower computation.
default_sigmas_num_sigmas.use_case: 8 is standard. Use 6 for faster testing, 10 for more thorough search.

default_sigmas_min_sigma.explanation: Minimum pRF size (sigma) to search in degrees of visual angle. Controls the smallest receptive field to consider.
default_sigmas_min_sigma.use_case: 0.5° is typical for early visual areas. Use larger values for later visual areas.

default_sigmas_max_sigma.explanation: Maximum pRF size (sigma) to search in degrees of visual angle. Controls the largest receptive field to consider.
default_sigmas_max_sigma.use_case: 5° is typical for early visual areas. Use larger values (7-10°) for later/higher visual areas.

nDCT.explanation: Number of DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) basis functions for modeling low-frequency drift in fMRI signal. Generates (2*nDCT + 1) regressors.
nDCT.use_case: 1 is standard and sufficient for most studies. Increase if you have significant low-frequency drift.

faqs.question: What is a population receptive field (pRF)?
faqs.answer: A pRF is the region of visual space that a voxel in visual cortex responds to. It's typically modeled as a 2D Gaussian. The pRF model estimates each voxel's preferred position (x, y) and size (sigma) in visual space, which reveals how visual cortex represents the visual world.

faqs.question: What is the difference between individual and concatenated run analysis?
faqs.answer: Individual: Analyzes each run separately, which is useful when runs have different stimulus conditions. Concatenated: Combines multiple runs before analysis, increasing statistical power by pooling more data. Use concatenated if your runs have the same stimulus to get more stable estimates.

faqs.question: Why should I enable refine fitting?
faqs.answer: Refine fitting uses optimization algorithms to fine-tune the initial grid search results, leading to more accurate pRF parameter estimates. It takes longer but produces better-quality results. Enable it for final analyses.

faqs.question: What should I set the batch size to?
faqs.answer: Start with 500. If you get GPU out-of-memory errors, decrease it (e.g., to 300). If you have a powerful GPU (>24GB VRAM) and want faster processing, increase it (e.g., to 1000). Larger batches use more memory but can be faster due to better GPU utilization.

faqs.question: How do I choose the spatial grid resolution?
faqs.answer: 51x51 is a good default. Use 41x41 for quick testing (faster but less detailed). Use 61x61 for final analysis requiring higher spatial resolution in visual space. Higher values increase computation time quadratically.

faqs.question: What stimulus parameters should I use?
faqs.answer: Visual field: should match your stimulus extent (typically 8° for standard stimuli). Width/Height: should match your stimulus image dimensions (typically 101x101 pixels). Enable binarization if your stimulus is noisy to convert it to binary 0/1 values.

faqs.question: What does visual field radius mean?
faqs.answer: It's the extent of the visual field in degrees (e.g., ±8° means the stimulus covers 16x16 degrees). Your spatial grid search space should be at least as large as your stimulus visual field to avoid missing pRFs at the boundaries.

faqs.question: When should I use GPU acceleration?
faqs.answer: Always enable GPU acceleration (refinefit_on_gpu=True) if you have a GPU with at least 8GB VRAM. GPUs are 10-100x faster than CPU for pRF fitting. Disable only if you have limited GPU memory or need reproducible CPU-based results.

faqs.question: What is BIDS format and why should I use it?
faqs.answer: BIDS (Brain Imaging Data Structure) is a standardized way to organize neuroimaging data. Using BIDS makes data sharing easier, enables automated analysis pipelines, and reduces errors from manual path management. GEM-pRF strongly recommends BIDS format.

faqs.question: How do I know which fMRI space to analyze?
faqs.answer: fsnative: subject's native surface space (good for individual analysis). fsaverage: standard template surface (good for group analysis). T1w: subject's native volumetric space. Choose based on your analysis goal and preprocessing results.

tips: Start with small batches (300) if you're unsure about GPU memory. You can always increase later.
Always validate your stimulus files are in the correct directory before running analysis.
Use 'all' for subjects/runs during initial testing to catch configuration errors early.
Keep results_overwrite=False until you're sure your configuration is correct.
Enable debug_info temporarily if analysis results look suspicious.
The configuration file is the most important part - get it right and GEM-pRF will run smoothly!
If you have multiple GPUs, add them to additional_available_gpus for parallel processing.
Consider using fsaverage for group-level statistics and retinotopic maps.
Make sure your stimulus visual field matches your actual stimulus extent.
For publication-quality pRF maps, use refine_fitting=True and higher spatial grid resolution (61x61).
